messages:
Tariq A.: Heads-up: onboarding new hires hit two redwoodctl problems today. 1) the curl install script fails on WSL when /usr/local is a symlink to a Windows mount, 2) our CI runners are getting wrong profile applied during `redwoodctl login`. Anyone seen both?

Leah C.: For (1) what's the failure? Did the script use `install -m` or try to write to /usr/local/bin directly?

Tariq A.: It prints `cannot create regular file '/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl': Permission denied` even when the user is in sudoers and we invoked with sudo. The underlying cause was the Windows mount not honoring chmod. The curl script doesn't check for destination writability or offer alternate paths.

Sam T.: We should update the installer to detect mountpoints and fall back to $HOME/.local/bin or suggest `--dest` flag. Quick workaround: `mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && curl ... | tar -xO > ~/.local/bin/redwoodctl && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/redwoodctl` and add ~/.local/bin to PATH.

Tariq A.: Added that to the new hire doc for now. Will file an issue to add `--dest` to the script.

Leah C.: About (2) the profile bug: CI jobs that mount a shared home keep an old `~/.redwood/config.toml` with duplicate profiles. `redwoodctl login --profile staging` attaches token to the first profile with that name rather than the intended endpoint. Repro is fast if you create two `[profile] name="staging"` tables.

Sam T.: That's because our matching is name-only. Short term: use `REDWOODCTL_CONFIG=/tmp/redwood-config` in CI to guarantee a clean config. Longer term: we should match on name+endpoint or generate unique profile ids on create.

build-bot: pipeline #8721: flake: integration step failed on `redwoodctl login` - token saved to wrong profile, subsequent steps used the wrong endpoint.

Leah C.: Filing issue and including a small Python repro that writes a TOML with two profile tables and runs `redwoodctl login --profile staging` to show token goes to the first table. Will propose adding a warning when duplicate names exist and a non-interactive flag `--profile-id` that accepts a deterministic id.

Sam T.: Also request: add `--no-browser` and `--token-stdin` for headless auth flows in CI. We currently support `--token-file` in master but it's not in release notes; docs need to show examples with CI secrets manager.

Tariq A.: I linked a short snippet in the onboarding doc: `cat /secrets/redwood | redwoodctl login --token-stdin --profile ci` — worked in our runner. Can we standardize the stdin flag name? Some people prefer `--token-stdin`, others `--token-file`.

Leah C.: Agree on standardizing. I'll consolidate in the issue: support `--token-file`, `--token-stdin`, `--no-browser`, and document `REDWOODCTL_CONFIG` usage. Also add installer fallback for non-writable dests.

redwoodctl-bot: New issue created: #2579 "installer: dest fallback for mountpoints; config profile matching + headless auth flags" by Leah C. https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/2579
